title: Maa Behen Is Now Streaming on Netflix. The Reviews Say Madhuri Dixit Just Delivered Her Best Performance in Years.
excerpt: Suresh Triveni's dark comedy about a mother-daughter trio covering up a crime has divided critics on its screenplay but united them on its cast. For the diaspora, it is the Madhuri Dixit comeback that Mrs Deshpande should have been.
body:
A dead body in a kitchen. A widow who works at a wine shop and wears sleeveless blouses. Two daughters who are as different from each other as they are from the neighbours who judge them. That is the setup of *Maa Behen*, Suresh Triveni's new dark comedy that premiered on Netflix on June 4 — and it is the kind of premise that Bollywood rarely trusts its biggest female stars with.

Madhuri Dixit plays Rekha, a fiercely non-conforming single mother in a Bihar housing colony. When her nosy, moral-policing neighbour Gupta Ji (Ravi Kishan) turns up dead in her home, Rekha calls her daughters Jaya (Triptii Dimri) and Sushma (Dharna Durga) for an emergency clean-up. What follows is two hours of escalating chaos — lies stacking on lies, suspicions spiralling, and three women trying to survive the biggest scandal their colony has ever seen.

## The Reviews Are Split Down the Middle

Critics have been generous with the cast and divided on the writing. India Forums gave it 3.5 out of 5, calling it a film that "uses chaos, humour and dysfunctional family dynamics to tell a story about women who have spent their lives being judged." Pinkvilla was less convinced at 2.5 out of 5, praising the visual direction — "Bihar has traditionally been shown in a very dull colour palette; contrary to that trope, *Maa Behen* is quite colourful" — but noting that the screenplay loses steam in the second half. MensXP landed at 3 out of 5, calling it "a decent entertainer with an outstanding Madhuri Dixit and Triptii Dimri leading the pack."

The social media verdict has been similarly polarised. One widely shared review described it as "one of the better Netflix films I've watched — big swings, clever writing, inventive design." Another called it a "snoozefest" where "the writing should get some maa behen gaali." A third praised the social messaging: "It's so refreshing to see a film openly address that specific kind of social policing."

## Madhuri's Real Comeback

The consensus, even among the film's detractors, is that Madhuri Dixit is extraordinary in it. After the widely panned *Mrs Deshpande*, her previous streaming effort, this feels like a course correction. MensXP put it bluntly: "She proves why she was once the top star and deserves to be seen more on our screens." Triptii Dimri continues her run of strong performances, and the surprise package is Dharna Durga — a digital creator making her film debut — who "manages to stand her own against a stalwart like Madhuri Dixit."

The film is written by Pooja Tolani and produced by Vikram Malhotra's Abundantia Entertainment. At 127 minutes, it does not overstay its welcome, even if the second hour sags. Ravi Kishan gets limited scope early on but reportedly makes the most of his screen time in the back half.

## What the Diaspora Should Know

For NRIs who have been waiting for a worthwhile Hindi film on Netflix, *Maa Behen* is a solid weekend pick — flawed but entertaining, with a lead performance from Madhuri Dixit that reminds you why she was once the most bankable name in Indian cinema. It is streaming globally right now, in Hindi with subtitles.

The film joins a growing list of Netflix India originals that are finding their audience among the diaspora. For a generation that grew up watching Madhuri in *Hum Aapke Hain Koun* and *Dil To Pagal Hai*, seeing her play a widow who refuses to conform to small-town expectations feels like the kind of role she should have been doing all along.

*Sources: India Forums, Pinkvilla, MensXP, social media reviews on X*
